plugins/transforms/aws/textract_client.p: The broad `except Exception` wraps only the telemetry emit callback, which runs AFTER the audit row has been durably recorded via `_record_call`. Telemetry is a Tier-3 best-effort sink: an exporter failure must not convert an already-audited, successful Textract call into a row failure. The handler is not a swallow-all: the two clauses above it re-raise `contract_errors.TIER_1_ERRORS` and the programming-error family (TypeError/AttributeError/KeyError/NameError), so only exporter-side runtime failures reach the warning path, and those are logged with `exc_info=True`, run_id, state_id and call_type so the loss is visible. This mirrors the identical `telemetry_emit_failed` discipline in infrastructure/clients/http.py and llm.py.

The `except TextractResponseError` handler does not swallow: it captures the exception into `terminal_error`, records the failure as the audit row's error payload (category, retryable=False) and telemetry, and the function re-raises `terminal_error` unconditionally after `_record_call`/`_emit_after_audit` (`if terminal_error is not None: raise terminal_error`). The deferral exists so a malformed provider response is AUDITED before it fails the row; the lint cannot see the raise because it lives after the try statement rather than inside the handler.

The botocore-exception handler (`_textract_provider_exception_types()`) classifies the vendor error through the `_provider_error` boundary into a sanitized `TextractServiceError` or `TextractIdempotencyInvariantError`, stores it in `terminal_error`, records the sanitized code/retryable/attempts on the audit row, and the function re-raises `terminal_error` after the audit write. Nothing is dropped: the raw botocore exception is replaced by an owned typed exception carrying only the bounded error code, and the raise is deferred solely so the audit row precedes the failure.

Same record-then-raise seam as start_document_analysis: `except TextractResponseError` assigns `terminal_error`, writes the malformed-response category to the audit row and telemetry, and the method ends with `if terminal_error is not None: raise terminal_error`. The handler defers the raise past the audit write; it never suppresses it.

Same record-then-raise seam for the botocore-exception clause on GetDocumentAnalysis: the vendor exception is parsed by the `_provider_error` boundary into an owned `TextractServiceError`/`TextractIdempotencyInvariantError`, audited with sanitized code and attempt count, and re-raised as `terminal_error` after `_record_call`/`_emit_after_audit`.

Same record-then-raise seam on the synchronous AnalyzeDocument path: `except TextractResponseError` stores the exception in `terminal_error`, audits the malformed-response category and attempt count, and the method re-raises `terminal_error` after the audit write. The deferral guarantees the audit row exists before the row fails.

Same record-then-raise seam for the botocore-exception clause on AnalyzeDocument: `_provider_error` (a non-raising Tier-3 boundary) sanitizes the vendor exception, the owned `TextractServiceError` is stored in `terminal_error`, the audit row records the bounded code/retryable/attempts, and `terminal_error` is re-raised after `_record_call`/`_emit_after_audit`. The idempotency-mismatch arm is deliberately collapsed here because AnalyzeDocument sends no token.
plugins/transforms/aws/textract_inline_a: `isinstance(document, TransformResult)` is nominal discrimination against `TransformResult`, a concrete class ELSPETH owns, over the Tier-2 union `_read_document_bytes` returns (`tuple[str, bytes] | TransformResult`): the early-return arm carries an already-built row error result, the other arm carries validated payload bytes. This is ADR-032 rule 1 (internal boundary: isinstance against an owned concrete class), not a Tier-3 shape guard, and neither arm defaults or coerces — a foreign object would fail the tuple unpack on the next line.
plugins/transforms/pdf_rasterize.py:R5:P: `isinstance(result, DocumentRefusal)` is nominal discrimination against an ELSPETH-owned frozen dataclass that is one member of the closed `RenderResult` union returned by the out-of-process renderer seam (see the 2026-08-25 pdf_rasterize entry in docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md). Each arm maps one owned variant to its TransformResult error; the fallthrough is the rendered-pages variant, which is then verified against `output_dir` and page-path containment, so nothing is defaulted. ADR-032 rule 1 prescribes exactly this isinstance-against-a-concrete-owned-class form for internal unions.

`isinstance(result, RenderTimedOut)` is the second nominal arm over the same owned `RenderResult` union: `RenderTimedOut` is an ELSPETH-owned frozen dataclass and the arm maps it to the non-retryable `render_timeout` row error carrying its own `timeout_seconds`. Nominal discrimination against a concrete owned class is ADR-032's internal-boundary control; no coercion or default is applied and the remaining variant is verified, not assumed.
